need: Admins and compliance teams need a reliable record of who changed what (permissions, deletions, logins) to answer audits and investigations.
Users need to find information that lives inside attached files, not only in task titles.
Users need to apply the same change to many existing tasks at once instead of editing them one by one.
People who plan their week in an external calendar need task deadlines to appear there.
Teams that coordinate in a chat tool need work requests and task updates to move between chat and Tasklane.
Firms want clients and outside collaborators to see the progress of their own work without full seats or access to other clients.
Teams need to capture their own structured attributes on tasks.
Users working in low light want a dark appearance that is comfortable for their eyes.
Firms need client data deleted automatically after a contractual retention period.
Developers need programmatic access so Tasklane can be automated and synchronised with internal systems.
Requests that arrive by email need to become tasks without retyping.
Customers with regulatory or contractual constraints need their data stored in a specific region (the EU).
Confidential financial information (rates, costs, budgets) must be visible only to authorised roles.
Teams migrating to Tasklane need to bring existing work in from spreadsheets or other tools.
Staff who are not fluent in English need the interface in their own language.
Finance staff need invoice data to reach their accounting system without manual re-entry or reconciliation.
Heavy daily users want to work faster without the mouse.
Users with low vision need sufficient contrast, scalable text and zoom support to read and use the app.
People away from their desk need to learn immediately when someone mentions or needs them.
Firms with international clients need to bill each client in that client's currency.
Users receive so many individual notifications that they ignore them; they need fewer, consolidated updates.
Field workers need to record time on mobile without connectivity and have it sync later.
Firms want clients to be able to pay invoices online so that money arrives sooner and with less manual work.
Firms need overdue invoices to be followed up reliably without staff writing chasing emails.
Project leads need early warning when a project is burning through its budgeted hours.
Teams want to start new projects from a standard, reusable structure instead of rebuilding or copying old ones.
People in distributed teams need protection from notifications outside their own working hours.
Users need a way to recover from accidental deletions and destructive mistakes.
Work that happens on a regular schedule should reappear automatically so it is not forgotten.
Time entries become wrong when people forget to stop timers; they need safeguards against runaway or idle time.
Users repeatedly rebuild the same filtered views and want to reuse them.
Managers and executives want recurring reports delivered to them automatically, without logging in or assembling them by hand.
Admins need sessions on shared or unattended computers to expire automatically.
IT needs Tasklane sign-in and access removal to be controlled centrally through the company identity provider.
Teams need to express that work depends on other work, so ordering is respected and the impact of delays is visible.
Plans need to account for people's absences so work isn't assigned to someone who is away.
Planners need to see and communicate a project schedule laid out over time.
Managers need to review and approve logged hours before they are billed.
Account owners need a second factor so that a stolen password alone cannot grant access.
Managers need to see how loaded each person is before assigning work, to avoid overload.
